_about: DevAscend knowledge base. Each topic = something worth learning. requires_any: you need at least ONE of these (survey skill names or topic ids). survey_skill: links the topic to the ML data (market value boost + trend). type: 'skill' (technology), 'essential' (workplace skill juniors usually discover late), 'trend' (where the market is going). level: when it is usually learned. core_for: roles for which this topic is a core skill (ranked higher).

topics.name: HTML/CSS
topics.why: The foundation of every web page. Everything in frontend builds on it.

topics.name: JavaScript
topics.why: The most used language in the survey; needed for any web work, frontend or backend (Node.js).

topics.name: Tailwind CSS
topics.why: You already know CSS. Tailwind lets you style much faster with utility classes, and it is the default in many new React / Next.js projects and job listings.

resources.title: Tailwind Play (try it in the browser)

topics.name: TypeScript
topics.why: JavaScript with types. It catches bugs before you run the code, and most professional JS teams now require it.

topics.name: React
topics.why: The most popular frontend library. Components, state and hooks are asked about in almost every frontend interview.

topics.name: Next.js
topics.why: The standard React framework for production: routing, server rendering, SEO and API routes in one place.

topics.name: State management & data fetching
topics.why: Real apps share data between many screens. Tools like TanStack Query and Redux Toolkit stop bugs from duplicated or outdated data.

topics.name: Form validation (client side)
topics.why: Every real app has forms: login, signup, checkout. At work you must validate input, show clear error messages and handle loading states. Tutorials usually skip this.

topics.name: Web accessibility (a11y)
topics.why: Your site must work with a keyboard and screen readers. Many companies are legally required to do this, and it is checked in code reviews.

topics.name: Web performance
topics.why: Slow sites lose users. Knowing Core Web Vitals, lazy loading and bundle size is what separates Mid from Junior frontend developers.

topics.name: Automated testing
topics.why: In a job, code is not 'done' until it has tests. Unit tests and end-to-end tests let a team change code without breaking things.

topics.name: Node.js
topics.why: Lets you use the JavaScript you already know on the server, which is the fastest path to becoming full-stack.

topics.name: Express
topics.why: The most common Node.js web framework for building REST APIs.

topics.name: REST API design
topics.why: Making an API that works is easy; making one other developers can use is a skill: correct HTTP status codes, consistent URLs, pagination and versioning.

resources.title: Microsoft: Web API design best practices

topics.name: Server-side validation & error handling
topics.why: Never trust data from the browser: anyone can bypass frontend checks. Juniors often forget this until a production bug or a security issue teaches them.
learn: Validate every request body (Zod / Joi / Pydantic / Bean Validation)
Never leak stack traces to users

topics.name: Authentication & authorization
topics.why: Almost every app has users. You need to know how passwords are hashed, how sessions and JWTs work, and how to check permissions.

topics.name: SQL
topics.why: One of the most used skills in the survey and needed in almost every backend and data job.

topics.name: PostgreSQL
topics.why: The most popular database among professional developers in recent surveys.

topics.name: Database design & indexing
topics.why: Bad table design and missing indexes are the most common reasons apps become slow as they grow.

topics.name: MongoDB
topics.why: Popular document database in the JavaScript (MERN) world.

topics.name: Redis & caching
topics.why: Caching is the first tool for making a slow backend fast. Redis is also used for sessions, queues and rate limiting.

topics.name: GraphQL
topics.why: An alternative to REST where the client asks for exactly the data it needs. It is common in larger frontend-heavy companies.

topics.name: Real-time apps (WebSockets)
topics.why: Chats, notifications and live dashboards need servers that push data to the browser instead of waiting for requests.

topics.name: Message queues (Kafka / RabbitMQ)
topics.why: Big systems split work into services that talk through queues. This is a typical Senior backend topic and is linked to higher pay in the survey data.

topics.name: Git & GitHub team workflow
topics.why: On day one at a job you work on branches, open pull requests, review code and resolve merge conflicts. Knowing only 'git add / commit / push' is not enough.

topics.name: Environment variables, config & secrets
topics.why: Apps run in development, staging and production with different settings. Putting passwords or API keys in code (or on GitHub) is one of the most common junior mistakes.

topics.name: Debugging & DevTools
topics.why: Most of a developer's time is spent reading and fixing code. Using breakpoints, the network tab and stack traces instead of console.log everywhere saves hours.

topics.name: Web security basics (OWASP Top 10)
topics.why: Every developer is responsible for security. XSS, SQL injection and broken access control are still the most common attacks.

topics.name: Clean code, code review & design patterns
topics.why: Code is read far more than it is written. Seniors are judged on code that others can understand and change safely.

resources.title: Refactoring Guru: design patterns and refactoring

topics.name: Logging, monitoring & production debugging
topics.why: When something breaks in production you can't attach a debugger. Good logs, metrics and alerts are how teams find problems.

topics.name: Linux & command line
topics.why: Servers run Linux. You will use the terminal for Git, Docker, deployments and debugging.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)

topics.name: Docker
topics.why: Packages your app so it runs the same everywhere. It is one of the most used tools among professional developers and appears in most backend job posts.

topics.name: CI/CD (GitHub Actions)
topics.why: Teams automatically test and deploy every change. Knowing how a pipeline works makes you much more useful in a team.
learn: Running tests on every pull request

topics.name: Cloud basics (AWS)
topics.why: The most used cloud platform. Knowing how to deploy and run apps in the cloud is strongly linked with higher pay in the data.

topics.name: Kubernetes
topics.why: Runs many containers reliably across many servers. It is a typical Senior and DevOps skill and is linked to higher market value.

topics.name: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform)
topics.why: Creates cloud servers and databases from code, so infrastructure is repeatable and reviewable.

topics.name: Data structures & algorithms
topics.why: Most product-company interviews (especially in India) include DSA rounds. It also helps you write faster code.

topics.name: System design
topics.why: Moving from Mid to Senior means designing whole systems, not just features. It is asked in almost every Senior interview.

topics.name: AI-assisted development
topics.why: Most professional developers now use AI coding tools. Using them well, and checking their output, is now a basic job skill.
learn: Using AI to explain unfamiliar code
Knowing when not to trust it

topics.name: Building AI / LLM features
topics.why: Companies are adding AI features (chatbots, search, summaries) to their products. Developers who can call LLM APIs, use embeddings and build RAG are in demand.

topics.name: Python
topics.why: The main language for data and AI, and popular for backends and automation.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python (Harvard)

topics.name: Machine learning fundamentals
topics.why: Understanding how models are trained and evaluated helps you build and judge AI features, and it is the entry to ML roles.

topics.name: Deep learning (PyTorch)
topics.why: Neural networks power modern AI. PyTorch is the most used deep learning framework in research and industry.

topics.name: Java
topics.why: Widely used in large companies and banks, especially for backend systems.

topics.name: Spring Boot
topics.why: The standard way to build Java backends in companies.

topics.name: Android with Kotlin & Jetpack Compose
topics.why: Kotlin is Google's preferred language for Android, and Jetpack Compose is the modern way to build Android UIs.

topics.name: Flutter
topics.why: One codebase for Android, iOS and web. Very popular with startups and in India.

topics.name: iOS with Swift & SwiftUI
topics.why: The native way to build iPhone apps. Needed if you target iOS users or Apple-focused companies.

resources.title: Hacking with Swift: 100 Days of SwiftUI

topics.name: React Native
topics.why: Build Android and iOS apps with the React you already know.

topics.name: Go
topics.why: Simple, fast language used for cloud and backend services (Docker and Kubernetes are written in Go). It is linked with higher salaries in the survey data.

topics.name: Writing docs & communicating in a team
topics.why: Clear READMEs, pull request descriptions, tickets and stand-up updates make you look senior quickly. This skill is rarely taught.
learn: Asking good questions (with what you tried)

topics.name: Follow a full career roadmap
topics.why: Community roadmaps show everything a role needs, so you can see what you don't know yet.
learn: Pick the roadmap for your role
